title: In memoir, Biden defends record on Gaza, laments failed Saudi-Israel normalization
author: Rosaleen Carroll
text:
In memoir, Biden defends record on Gaza, laments failed Saudi-Israel normalization

The former US president said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu went “too far” in Gaza, and sought to explain his relations with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, despite promises of accountability over Jamal Khashoggi's murder.

Rosaleen Carroll

,

Adam Lucente

The new book 'Promise Me, America' by former US President Joe Biden is displayed at Skylight Books on Nov. 17, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. — Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

In his new memoir, former US President Joe Biden defended his support of Israel during the Gaza war while acknowledging behind-the-scenes tensions with Israeli leadership, and reflected on his unsuccessful normalization push in the region. Published Tuesday, Promise Me, America examines the competing priorities that shaped Biden’s Middle East policy on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, diplomacy with Iran, US-Saudi ties and more. Private strain, public support for Netanyahu governmentBiden described his handling of Israel’s military campaign in Gaza as a balance of private pressure on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu alongside continued US military and diplomatic backing for Israel.
